question: Should spawned-session chains use a new durable chain identifier distinct from the existing W3C diagnostic `traceId`, and which authorized session projections should expose it?
rationale: The identifier lifetime, naming, persistence, and public exposure change the session API contract and cannot safely be selected from implementation evidence alone.

options.title: Dedicated chain ID
options.body: Add a clearly named persisted chain identifier with root, parent, and depth fields on authorized lineage projections.

options.title: Parent and depth only
options.body: Persist parent and depth, derive roots when needed, and avoid introducing another durable identifier.

options.title: Reuse diagnostic tracing
options.body: Persist W3C trace IDs across session lifetimes, intentionally coupling request observability to session lineage.

recommendation.title: Dedicated chain ID
recommendation.body: Add a clearly named persisted chain identifier with root, parent, and depth fields on authorized lineage projections.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent history across the affected surfaces and already supplied the item-specific contract assessment.
